subject: Post-demo recap: latency measurement windows, concurrency gates, and remedies
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lisa Monroe <lisa@heritagehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-07T15:02:00Z
Subject: Post-demo recap: latency measurement windows, concurrency gates, and remedies

Hi Lisa — great demo earlier, thanks for the time. Quick recap and suggested next steps based on what we heard on the call: 

Summary notes from today's demo:
- Primary workload: streaming transcriptions for telehealth consults (avg call length 12–18 min).
- Peak concurrent streams observed in your pilot: ~180 streams during weekday mornings; steady-state 30–60.
- Target user-facing latency: must feel instant for agents — you mentioned P95 < 300ms for short-turn responses and P99 goals for end-of-chunk delivery.
- Important exclusions: scheduled maintenance windows and your site-level network outages (you called these out as outside vendor scope).

What we propose as the initial qualification and contract language to move to procurement: 
1) Measurement windows: compute token-level latency and an end-to-end chunk RTT. For the SLA we recommend: P95 token latency measured at the Redwood edge over 1-minute rolling windows, reported hourly; P99 chunk RTT measured per-call, aggregated daily.
2) Concurrency gates and burst: dedicate a concurrency reservation for steady-state (your committed concurrency: 200) with an automatic burst pool that allows +30% for 10-minute bursts. Bursts above that will be throttled with 429s and clearly reported.
3) Remedies & credits: standard service credit ladder tied to monthly availability of the committed concurrency pool and P95/P99 thresholds. We can propose a 5% credit for breach of P95 target in a monthly evaluation, 10% for repeated breaches.
4) Exclusions: scheduled maintenance (48h notice), customer network incidents, and force majeure. We'll also include a clear measurement exclusion for sustained DDoS or upstream provider outages.

Attachments: I've added a short proposal doc (latency-metrics-proposal.pdf) and the demo recording (demo-recording.mp4) for your team.

Next steps (proposed):
- Lisa: confirm whether the committed concurrency target should be 200 or 250; also confirm acceptable reporting cadence (hourly dashboards + daily executive digest).
- Redwood (Ben/Karthik): produce a one-page SLA draft that includes the measurement definitions above and a simple service-credit formula, share by EOD Thursday.
- Schedule: sync with Procurement after the SLA draft is shared — Lisa suggested next Wed for procurement review.

If that plan looks right I'll circulate the SLA draft and a short appendix that describes streaming measurement specifics (how we define chunk RTT vs token latency).

Thanks,
Sergio Alvarez
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-10-08T09:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: latency measurement windows, concurrency gates, and remedies

Thanks, Sergio — solid recap. A few clarifying questions from Procurement and our infra lead before you draft formal language: 

1) Measurement timing: when you say 'P95 token latency measured at the Redwood edge' — can you confirm this excludes client-side rendering time? We need the SLA to reflect server-side measurement only.
2) Chunk RTT: is that measured from when we push a chunk to your API to when the final token of that chunk is returned to our server (server-to-server), or from the agent UI perspective? We prefer server-to-server.
3) Bursts: the +30% for 10 minutes sounds reasonable; procurement asks what happens if a sustained burst lasts 2+ hours (e.g., a marketing event) — would we be blocked or can we request temporary capacity increases?
4) Remedies: procurement wants a formula that scales with committed spend. If the committed concurrency pool is 200 and we pay for that, credits should be tied to that commitment.

Also: we need to see an explicit exclusion clause for 3rd-party CDN/network provider outages and a clear path for dispute resolution (who decides measurement interpretation).

Procurement would like a draft SLA they can circulate to legal. Can you include a single-paragraph non-technical summary at the top of the draft for legal to skim?

Thanks — Lisa
Lisa Monroe
Head of Technology Operations
Heritage Health

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lisa Monroe <lisa@heritagehealth.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@heritagehealth.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: latency measurement windows, concurrency gates, and remedies

Hi all — looping in some proposed wording and measurement methodology so Sergio has something concrete to send to legal/procurement. High level approach below; I've attached a full draft (slo-draft-heritage.docx).

Measurement definitions (recommended):
- Token latency (server-side): time between Redwood receiving a token generation request and the server completing the generation of that token (does not include client rendering or network RTT from agent UI). Measured at the Redwood ingress point; aggregated per-customer. P95 target computed over 1-minute rolling windows and reported hourly.
- Chunk RTT (server-to-server): for streaming calls that submit chunks, measure from the RFC-validated chunk POST arrival at Redwood to the final chunk-complete event sent to the customer server. Per-call P99 aggregated daily.

Concurrency and burst policy (operational):
- Committed concurrency pool: customer pays for N reserved concurrent slots (recommended starting point: 200).
- Burst pool: temporary, auto-allocated spare capacity of up to +30% of the committed pool for up to 10 consecutive minutes.
- Extended burst: customer can request an on-demand capacity increase (subject to capacity availability and pricing) for events longer than 10 minutes; requests should be made via the Console or Account Manager.

Exclusions & dispute process:
- Exclusions: scheduled maintenance (48h notice), customer network outages, third-party provider failures (CDN, cloud provider), and force majeure. Sustained DDoS and upstream provider outages will be excluded from SLA calculations.
- Measurement disputes: Redwood will publish raw measurement logs to a secure shared S3/drive link for the disputed period; both parties agree to a 10-business-day review window. If unresolved, an independent third-party auditor (mutually agreed) can be engaged.

Remedies (sample ladder):
- If monthly P95 token latency >= target for > 1% of measured windows: 2% service credit on monthly invoice.
- If monthly P95 token latency >= target for > 5% of measured windows OR P99 chunk RTT breaches target in > 2% of calls: 5% credit.
- Repeated monthly violations escalate per contractual terms; credits capped at 20% per month.

Action items from Redwood:
- Sergio/Karthik: produce a non-technical one-paragraph summary + the docx SLA draft with the sections above (I attached the draft).
- Lisa: confirm committed concurrency and whether you prefer hourly/daily reporting cadence for the executive digest.

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: latency measurement windows, concurrency gates, and remedies

Lisa — thanks for the precise asks. Quick clarifications inline and a proposed timeline: 

- Server-side measurement confirmed: token latency excludes client rendering. We'll state this explicitly in the top summary for Legal.
- Chunk RTT definition: we'll measure server-to-server arrival-to-final-chunk-delivery (not UI). I'll add an appendix describing sample traces so your infra team can validate.
- Sustained bursts: we'll offer two paths — temporary on-demand capacity (paid) or a short-term expansion to the reserved pool (pricing to be agreed). I'll include both options in the SLA appendix and price them separately.
- Dispute process: agree with Ben's wording. We'll add an item describing the data export (raw logs) format and retention (90 days standard, extended available as an add-on).

Proposed timeline:
- Thu 2026-10-14 EOD: Redwood shares final one-paragraph summary + SLA draft (including appendix and pricing options).
- Wed 2026-10-20: Procurement review call (Heritage + Redwood).
- Following week: Procurement/Legal redlines and DocuSign routing.

I'll prepare the one-paragraph summary now and attach the SLA draft as promised. If that timeline works, I can schedule the procurement call for Oct 20.

Thanks — Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
